title: Local workspace and learning baseline
prerequisites: None; begin with the orientation tasks.
study: Local shell/editor/repository orientation; study-day versus calendar-day planning; synthetic data, cost limits and cleanup. Read a worked example before installing or using unfamiliar tools. Cloud account setup is Day 18; Terraform and Kubernetes are introduced when needed.
practice: Create a disposable Linux workspace and evidence repository; run one harmless command and record its exit code. Choose a lab budget and a cleanup checklist before enabling paid resources.
exit_evidence: A versioned README with available study hours, environment, baseline skills, budget and cleanup owner.

title: IP addressing and packet paths
study: OSI and TCP/IP models (what lives at each layer; L4 vs L7); IPv4 addressing, private ranges (RFC 1918), ARP/NDP, CIDR notation and subnet math (/24, /20, /16; splitting ranges); Packet lifecycle from physical NIC to application socket
practice: Split a /24 into four equal networks and trace a packet from a host to a different subnet using a supplied diagram.
exit_evidence: Four correct ranges with network/broadcast addresses and a labeled next-hop path.

title: DNS, sockets and transport
study: IPv6 basics; DNS: record types (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, SOA, PTR), TTL, recursive vs authoritative resolvers; TCP vs UDP, three-way handshake, TCP connection states (ESTABLISHED, TIME_WAIT), ports, socket buffers
practice: Trace an IPv4 and IPv6 lookup from supplied resolver output; label socket endpoints and the TCP handshake.
exit_evidence: A DNS/transport diagram distinguishing name resolution, reachability and established connection.

title: TLS, HTTP, MTU and routing vocabulary
study: HTTP/HTTPS, TLS 1.3 handshake, certificate validation chains, status codes, HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3; MTU and MSS clamping; NAT (SNAT/DNAT) for private outbound; Routing basics: static vs dynamic routing, BGP at conceptual level
practice: Compare a valid and a hostname-mismatched certificate trace; annotate an MTU failure and forward/return routes on supplied captures.
exit_evidence: A failure worksheet that separates TLS trust, packet size, routing and HTTP errors.

title: VPN, load balancers and firewalls
study: VPN concepts: IPsec, IKEv2 tunnels, site-to-site vs client VPN; Load balancing concepts: L4 vs L7, health checks, session affinity; Firewalls: stateful vs stateless, allow/deny rule ordering, failure boundaries
practice: Draw a client-to-backend flow with health checks and ordered firewall decisions; change one rule and predict the effect.
exit_evidence: A packet decision table with both allowed and denied paths and a failure boundary.

title: Shell, processes and services
study: Linux kernel vs user space, file system navigation, permissions (chmod, chown), users and groups; Processes, file descriptors (stdin/stdout/stderr), pipes, redirection, boot-to-service sequence and services (systemd unit lifecycle), signals (SIGTERM, SIGKILL), exit statuses, logs (journalctl, /var/log)
practice: Start and stop a disposable local service, inspect its PID and journal, and compare a graceful stop with a forced termination.
exit_evidence: Commands, exit codes and log timestamps explaining the service lifecycle.

title: SSH, scripts and process inspection
study: SSH: keys, config files, port forwarding, bastion (jump) hosts; Package managers (apt, yum/dnf); Shell scripting: variables, loops, conditionals, exit codes; /proc virtual filesystem and process trees
practice: Use a local test VM to inspect SSH configuration; write a small script that parses synthetic JSON and fails explicitly on invalid input.
exit_evidence: A script with successful and failed runs, quoting explained, and no stored credentials.

title: CPU, memory and diagnostic signals
study: CPU scheduling and waiting, context switching, virtual memory, page faults, RAM/page cache/swap, OOM and PSI; grep/sed/awk/jq and curl/dig/ss/tcpdump as diagnostic tools. Learn to interpret one signal at a time; advanced scheduler or kernel tuning is optional.
practice: Observe a bounded local CPU task and inspect memory/page-cache metrics; explain supplied OOM and PSI examples without exhausting the host.
exit_evidence: A resource baseline and predicted CPU-throttling versus memory-pressure symptoms.

title: VM and container isolation
study: Virtualization and Containers: Hypervisors (Type 1 vs Type 2), what a VM actually is; Containers vs VMs (Linux kernel namespaces: PID, net, mnt, IPC, UTS, user; cgroups v2 resource limits for CPU/memory; seccomp profiles and capabilities)
practice: Inspect a local container's namespaces, cgroup limits and user identity; compare its isolation boundary with a VM diagram.
exit_evidence: An isolation worksheet distinguishing resource enforcement from security isolation.

title: Images, filesystems and orchestration
study: Docker: images, layers, Dockerfile, registries, mounts, inodes, volumes, POSIX filesystem sync/fsync semantics; Container orchestration: why Kubernetes exists; Kubernetes core objects: Pod, Deployment, Service, Ingress, ConfigMap, Secret
practice: Build a tiny container from an annotated example; compare ephemeral files with a mounted volume and trace buffered write versus durable flush.
exit_evidence: A runnable image, persistence check and Pod/Deployment/Service ownership diagram.

title: Cloud service models and responsibility
study: IaaS, PaaS, FaaS, SaaS, and where GCP services fall; Shared responsibility model (what Google secures vs what you secure)
practice: Assign OS patching, application security and data recovery responsibilities for VM, managed-container and SaaS examples.
exit_evidence: A responsibility matrix with an owner for each task.

title: Regions, scaling and economics
study: Regions, zones, multi-region and edge locations; Elasticity vs scalability, vertical vs horizontal scaling; CapEx vs OpEx, pay-as-you-go economics
practice: Estimate two deployment locations and compare vertical versus horizontal scaling for the retailer's hypothetical workload.
exit_evidence: A location decision with latency, residency, cost and failure-domain assumptions.

title: State, availability and recovery vocabulary
study: High availability vs fault tolerance vs disaster recovery (three different things); Stateless vs stateful applications (this decides almost every HA design)
practice: Restart the local service with and without external state; distinguish an available replica from a recoverable backup.
exit_evidence: A state ownership diagram and definitions of HA, fault tolerance, RTO and RPO with examples.

title: Git, APIs and JSON
study: Git fundamentals (branch, merge, PR); REST APIs and JSON
practice: Commit a tiny request/response example; create a branch, review a diff and merge a change; parse an error response.
exit_evidence: A repository history and annotated HTTP/JSON success and failure examples.

title: Small application and architecture styles
study: Basic Python or Bash from an annotated example; request validation, REST/JSON, request IDs and structured logs. Compare monolith, microservices and serverless styles and apply relevant 12-factor principles. SQL starts on Day 16 rather than being bundled into this programming session.
practice: Adapt a worked Python or Bash example into a small order endpoint with request IDs and structured logs; handle invalid input.
exit_evidence: A reproducible local request, validation failure and a diagram comparing monolith and service boundaries.

title: SQL foundations and business outcomes
study: Relational tables, primary/foreign keys, normalization, SELECT/JOIN/GROUP BY and transaction commit/rollback. Introduce ACID and an isolation anomaly through a worked example; locking/deadlocks are practised on Day 61. Use Cloud Digital Leader material for business framing; its exam and full course are optional.
practice: Create local orders and customers tables with keys; run a join and aggregate; commit and roll back a transaction. Write the business outcome this application serves.
exit_evidence: Schema, query results, rollback evidence and a one-paragraph value statement; explain normalization and an isolation anomaly from a worked example.

title: Gate 1 — Foundation recall and repair
study: Review and remediate prior material only; use the matching gate criteria in the Gates section. Do not introduce new services or concepts on a checkpoint day.
practice: Reproduce the local request flow and SQL rollback without copying the walkthrough; repair the weakest shell, network or state explanation.
exit_evidence: A scored G1 checklist, corrected evidence and an explicit pass or repeat decision.

title: Cloud sandbox and cost controls
study: Create a GCP account, claim the free trial credit; Understand the free tier (Always Free products and their limits); Google Cloud Console tour (navigation, pinned products, project picker)
practice: Select a training sandbox or disposable project, inspect billing access and configure budget notifications if authorized.
exit_evidence: A redacted project/billing preflight and cleanup plan; explain why an alert is not a hard spend cap.

title: CLI configuration and identity checks
study: Cloud Shell (persistent 5 GB home directory, preinstalled tools); Install and configure `gcloud` locally (`gcloud init`, `gcloud config`, named configurations for multiple projects); Other CLIs: `gsutil`/`gcloud storage`, `bq`, `kubectl`
practice: Create named CLI configurations and verify project, identity and region before a read-only API call.
exit_evidence: Commands that reliably identify the target environment and prevent an accidental project switch.

title: APIs, client libraries and emulators
study: API enablement, client libraries, local versus cloud endpoints, Cloud Shell Editor/Cloud Code and asynchronous operation polling. Run one emulator; learn the purpose and documented limitations of Pub/Sub, Firestore, Spanner and Bigtable emulators without installing all four.
practice: Run one Pub/Sub emulator example; configure its client endpoint and document how Firestore, Spanner and Bigtable emulators differ from production.
exit_evidence: One reproducible emulator run and a four-service limitations matrix; no requirement to deploy all four.

title: Resource hierarchy and ownership
study: Organization node (tied to Cloud Identity or Google Workspace domain); Folders (mapping to departments, environments or teams); Projects: project ID vs project name vs project number (ID is immutable and globally unique)
practice: Sketch an organization/folder/project hierarchy for development and production and label each owner.
exit_evidence: A landing-zone draft with stable IDs, environment boundaries and operating responsibilities.

title: Inheritance, labels and tags
study: Resources and inheritance (policies flow downward and are additive for IAM); Labels vs tags vs network tags (three different things, often confused)
practice: Evaluate effective access in a sample parent/child hierarchy and choose labels versus policy tags versus network tags for three uses.
exit_evidence: An inheritance calculation and a tagging convention with concrete examples.

title: Organization policies and lifecycle
study: Project lifecycle: creation, shutdown, 30-day recovery window; Designing a hierarchy for prod/staging/dev and for multi-team companies; Organization Policy Service (constraints that restrict what can be done, regardless of IAM)
practice: Review a supplied policy plan that restricts location or external addresses; predict accepted and rejected resources before applying a sandbox example.
exit_evidence: An expected/observed or simulated policy test with rollback and a project lifecycle diagram.

title: Principals and workforce identity
study: Cloud Identity vs Google Workspace vs consumer Google accounts; Principals: Google account, group, service account, domain, allAuthenticatedUsers, allUsers; Why groups (not individual users) should receive roles
practice: Build a principal inventory for developers, operators and workloads; replace individual grants with suitable groups in the design.
exit_evidence: An identity matrix distinguishing people, service accounts, groups and external identities.

title: Roles and authorization decisions
study: Roles: basic (Owner/Editor/Viewer, avoid in production), predefined, custom; IAM policy structure: bindings, members, roles, conditions; Policy inheritance and the effective policy
practice: Evaluate predefined versus custom roles and test one narrow allowed operation and one denied operation using a sandbox or policy fixture.
exit_evidence: Redacted authorization evidence tied to principal, resource, role and condition.

title: Credentials, tokens and impersonation
study: Service accounts, least privilege, attached identity, impersonation and key avoidance; ADC resolution at introductory depth, metadata service, access versus ID tokens, audience and expiry. Full federation design returns on Days 100 and 166.
practice: Use a worked impersonation example; trace ADC lookup, token expiry and audience, and contrast attached workload identity with a saved key.
exit_evidence: An authentication flow separating authentication from authorization and access tokens from ID tokens; never save tokens.

title: Billing roles and budget ownership
study: Billing accounts vs projects (many projects can link to one billing account); Billing roles (Billing Account Administrator vs User vs Viewer); **Set budgets and alerts first** (thresholds at 50%, 90%, 100%)
practice: Map who can link projects, view spend and manage budgets; calculate alert thresholds for the lab budget.
exit_evidence: A billing responsibility matrix and correctly calculated thresholds.

title: Cost attribution and notifications
study: Programmatic budget notifications via Pub/Sub; Labels for cost attribution
practice: Route a sample budget notification through a local consumer or supplied trace and assign costs using project/label dimensions.
exit_evidence: An attribution worksheet and notification handling behavior for duplicate events.

title: Cost exports, quota and capacity
study: Billing reports and cost table; Billing export to BigQuery; Understanding quotas (rate quotas vs allocation quotas) and how to request increases
practice: Read a sample billing export and distinguish rate limits, allocation quotas and actual resource availability.
exit_evidence: A cost query or spreadsheet plus three different capacity-failure explanations.

title: Region and resource-scope decisions
study: Regions and zones: how to pick one (latency, cost, compliance, service availability, carbon footprint); Zonal vs regional vs multi-regional vs global resources
practice: Compare two candidate regions and label each resource as zonal, regional, multi-regional or global using current documentation.
exit_evidence: A location/scope matrix with service availability and residency checks.

title: Network tiers and delivery paths
study: Google's private global network and edge points of presence; Network Service Tiers (Premium vs Standard); Service availability differs by region (always check)
practice: Draw two client delivery paths and compare documented Premium/Standard trade-offs against the same traffic assumptions.
exit_evidence: A network-tier ADR that identifies pricing and behavior needing current verification.

title: Support, inventory and learning tracker
study: Support plans and escalation, Cloud Asset Inventory, public status and Personalized Service Health. Introduce the topic tracker, six-domain exam map and Google Skills learning resources; maintain them throughout the course.
practice: Inventory the sandbox or a supplied asset snapshot; create an 83-topic tracker and locate current exam objectives and support escalation channels.
exit_evidence: An asset list, topic-to-evidence tracker and incident contact/escalation sheet.

title: Lifecycle policies and operating assumptions
study: SLA versus SLO, launch stage, deprecation notices and service lifecycle; review the hierarchy and budget artifacts already created. Define an owner and exit/migration trigger for each chosen service.
practice: Review launch stage and deprecation notices for two chosen services; define migration triggers and resource expiration rules.
exit_evidence: A service lifecycle register with owner, review date and an exit option.

title: First controlled cloud resource operation
study: Observe control-plane versus data-plane behavior, asynchronous operations, desired versus observed state and permission propagation; create, inventory and delete one small VM using gcloud. Retry only after classifying the error and checking the operation state.
practice: Create one disposable VM through the CLI, observe its asynchronous operation, inventory it and delete it after recording the evidence.
exit_evidence: A creation/deletion trace, active-identity checks and empty-resource confirmation; a supplied trace is acceptable when access is unavailable.

title: Gate 2 — Sandbox and identity readiness
study: Review and remediate prior material only; use the matching gate criteria in the Gates section. Do not introduce new services or concepts on a checkpoint day.
practice: Repeat the environment preflight, demonstrate narrow access and a denial, and verify inventory and cleanup without the original walkthrough.
exit_evidence: A scored G2 checklist, budget/identity evidence and resolved critical access or cleanup gaps.

title: VM sizing and image choices
study: Compare currently available general-purpose, compute-optimized, memory-optimized, HPC and accelerator families using current documentation; Custom machine types and extended memory; Shared-core vs standard machine types; Boot disks, images (public, custom, image families), snapshots and machine images
practice: Choose a small VM for the local order service using CPU/memory measurements and compare two image/machine choices on paper.
exit_evidence: A sizing sheet with workload assumptions, customer-managed layers and one rejected option.

title: Disks, metadata and persistence
study: Persistent Disk types (standard, balanced, SSD, extreme), Hyperdisk, Local SSD (ephemeral); Zonal vs regional persistent disks; Startup scripts and metadata server
practice: Attach a small test volume or use a local equivalent; restart the application, verify data persistence and inspect a redacted metadata flow.
exit_evidence: Persistence evidence and a block-storage comparison that distinguishes ephemeral from durable data.

title: Templates, MIGs and scaling
study: Instance templates and Managed Instance Groups (MIGs); Zonal vs regional MIGs; Autoscaling policies (CPU, load balancing utilization, custom metrics, schedules)
practice: Create a minimal template or review a supplied plan; predict instance count for a short load trace under two scaling policies.
exit_evidence: A template and scaling timeline with stated cooldown and capacity assumptions.

title: Autohealing and deployment changes
study: Autohealing with health checks; Rolling updates: max surge, max unavailable, canary rollouts; Stateful MIGs; Unmanaged instance groups
practice: Inject an unhealthy response in a bounded MIG lab or replay health-check traces; compare autohealing with autoscaling and rolling replacement.
exit_evidence: A recovery timeline with readiness, max-surge and unavailability constraints.

title: Spot, tenancy and secure VM access
study: Preemptible/Spot workload fit, documented interruption behavior and checkpoint/restart handling; Sole-tenant nodes and licensing (BYOL); Shielded VMs and Confidential VMs; OS Login and SSH key management
practice: Simulate a shutdown notice and checkpoint the worker; compare Spot, standard and sole-tenant choices and explain OS Login access.
exit_evidence: A restartable worker trace and runtime/security decision sheet with documented interruption assumptions.

title: VM operations and resource diagnosis
study: VM Manager (patching, inventory, OS config); Live migration and maintenance policies (migrate vs terminate); Sustained use discounts, committed use discounts, rightsizing recommendations
practice: Revisit CPU and memory symptoms on the service; inspect a patch/maintenance plan and document a safe rollback.
exit_evidence: A VM runbook linking guest metrics to application symptoms and a maintenance decision.

title: Kubernetes architecture and cluster choices
study: Kubernetes architecture: control plane, nodes, etcd, kubelet, kube-proxy; Autopilot vs Standard mode (when to choose each); Zonal vs regional clusters (regional for HA control plane)
practice: Run a local cluster example or use a sandbox and trace desired versus observed Deployment state through scheduler, controller and kubelet.
exit_evidence: A reconciliation diagram and an Autopilot-versus-Standard ownership comparison.

title: Scheduling, scaling and Kubernetes access
study: Node pools, requests/limits, scheduling, taints/tolerations, HPA/VPA and node autoscaling; Kubernetes RBAC versus IAM. Recognize Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job and CronJob and compare Service/Ingress/Gateway roles; use one workload for practice rather than deploying every object.
practice: Set requests/limits on a tiny workload; deliberately create a Pending pod and diagnose the scheduling reason. Compare a Kubernetes RBAC denial with IAM.
exit_evidence: Events and a corrected manifest, plus an HPA/node-scaling diagram and authorization distinction.

title: Service networking and persistent volumes
study: Container-native load balancing (NEGs); VPC-native clusters, alias IPs, private clusters, authorized networks; Storage: PersistentVolumes, PersistentVolumeClaims, StorageClasses
practice: Trace Pod-to-Service traffic and a PVC binding using a local cluster or annotated GKE trace; compare documented CNI/Dataplane V2 paths.
exit_evidence: A packet/storage diagram with managed-service boundaries and no claims about hidden implementation details.

title: Probes, secrets and workload failures
study: Config and secrets: ConfigMaps, Secrets, Secret Manager integration; Workload Identity Federation for GKE; Network Policies and Dataplane V2; Release channels and upgrade strategies (surge upgrades, maintenance windows); Startup vs readiness vs liveness probes; troubleshoot CrashLoopBackOff and OOMKilled using kubectl describe, logs, events and resource metrics.
practice: Use isolated fixtures for a failing startup probe, crash loop and memory-limit termination; correct one live/local failure and explain the others from traces.
exit_evidence: A diagnostic decision tree, corrected probe/resource settings and a secret-access boundary.

title: Fleet, supply chain and mesh trade-offs
study: Fleet/Enterprise concepts, Connect Gateway, Config Sync, Policy Controller and multi-cluster service/ingress boundaries. Recognize image scanning and Binary Authorization before their labs on Days 114–115. Compare service-mesh identity/mTLS and traffic policy with direct service communication; evaluate cost and operational overhead.
practice: Review two cluster/fleet designs and a service-mesh request path; explain mTLS identity, policy and operating costs without installing a production mesh.
exit_evidence: A runtime ADR with fleet/mesh alternatives and links to the scheduling/isolation evidence from Days 43–45.

title: Cloud Run and event-driven functions
study: **Cloud Run:** services vs jobs, revisions, traffic splitting, concurrency, min/max instances, CPU allocation, VPC connectivity (Direct VPC egress, connectors), custom domains, authentication and invokers; **Cloud Run functions (Cloud Functions):** event-driven triggers, gen1 vs gen2, cold starts, timeouts, event sources (Pub/Sub, Storage, Eventarc)
practice: Deploy the small service to one managed runtime or use an approved sandbox; test concurrency, authentication and a bad revision rollback.
exit_evidence: A revision/request trace and scaling/identity settings; compare functions/jobs as alternatives.

title: Workflows and runtime selection
study: **App Engine:** Standard vs Flexible, services and versions, traffic splitting (know when not to use it for new builds); Eventarc, Cloud Scheduler, Cloud Tasks, Workflows (serverless orchestration); Choosing between Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud Run, Functions and App Engine (see cheat sheets)
practice: Use a small local workflow or supplied Workflows sample to coordinate two steps and handle one failure; compare App Engine, Tasks, Scheduler and Eventarc roles.
exit_evidence: A retry/failure diagram and runtime decision matrix grounded in the earlier VM/container/serverless evidence.

title: VPC address and route design
study: VPC as a global resource; subnets as regional resources; Auto mode vs custom mode VPCs and controlled enterprise IP planning; Subnet IP ranges, secondary ranges (for GKE pods and services), expanding ranges; Routes: system-generated, custom static, dynamic (Cloud Router with BGP), route priority
practice: Allocate non-overlapping subnet and secondary ranges; build a custom VPC or validate a supplied plan and evaluate route selection.
exit_evidence: An IP plan and forward/return packet path with route priorities.

title: Firewall policy and private API access
study: Firewall rules: direction, priority, targets (tags and service accounts), implied rules, logging; Hierarchical firewall policies and network firewall policies; External vs internal IP addresses; ephemeral vs static; reserved addresses; Private Google Access and Private Service Connect
practice: Test or simulate one permitted and one blocked connection; compare Private Google Access with Private Service Connect.
exit_evidence: A firewall decision trace and identity/network boundary diagram.

title: Peering, Shared VPC, PSC and NAT
study: Private services access (PSA) vs Private Service Connect (PSC endpoints, PSC service attachments, PSC interfaces; check endpoint/interface address requirements and overlapping-address constraints for the selected PSC pattern); VPC Network Peering (non-transitive, no overlapping ranges); Shared VPC (host and service projects, the enterprise landing zone baseline); Cloud NAT (Private NAT, gateway endpoints; no inbound)
practice: Trace one private-service path and one outbound NAT path, including return routing, translation state and ephemeral-port demand.
exit_evidence: A PSC/PSA/peering comparison and a NAT exhaustion hypothesis with measurable signals.

title: DNS, hybrid transit and network diagnosis
study: Cloud DNS: public and private zones, forwarding, peering zones, DNSSEC, response policies; Network Connectivity Center (NCC as enterprise transit hub connecting VPC spokes, hybrid links, and SD-WAN router appliances); VPC Flow Logs, Firewall Rules Logging, Packet Mirroring; Network Intelligence Center (Connectivity Tests, Network Topology, Performance Dashboard)
practice: Reproduce a DNS error locally; use a sandbox Connectivity Test or supplied route logs to distinguish DNS, firewall and transit faults.
exit_evidence: A network runbook and NCC topology with explicit peering/transit limitations.

title: Load-balancer architecture
study: Load balancer taxonomy: global vs regional, external vs internal, proxy vs passthrough, L4 vs L7; Global external Application Load Balancer (HTTP/S): URL maps, backend services, backend buckets, host and path rules; Regional external and internal Application Load Balancers; External and internal proxy Network Load Balancers (TCP/SSL proxy)
practice: Choose a load balancer for the order service and label frontend, proxy or passthrough behavior, backend and health-check paths.
exit_evidence: A selection ADR comparing two feasible load-balancer types.

title: Health checks, certificates and draining
study: Passthrough Network Load Balancers (external and internal); Health checks (protocols, intervals, thresholds; firewall rules needed for health check ranges); Session affinity, connection draining, timeouts; SSL certificates: Google-managed, self-managed, Certificate Manager, SSL policies
practice: Break a local readiness endpoint or certificate fixture, then restore it; walk connection draining during a rollout.
exit_evidence: A timestamped failure/recovery trace and certificate/health-check ownership checklist.

title: CDN, WAF and traffic management
study: Cloud CDN (cache modes, cache keys, invalidation, signed URLs); Cloud Armor (WAF rules, rate limiting, geo and IP allow/deny lists, adaptive protection); Traffic management: weighted traffic splitting, header-based routing, cross-region failover; Choosing the right load balancer (decision tree in cheat sheets)
practice: Test cache-key behavior locally or from supplied headers; analyze a WAF false-positive fixture and model weighted routing.
exit_evidence: A cache/security decision with invalidation, rollback and observability requirements.

title: Hybrid topology and failure domains
study: Cloud VPN: Classic vs HA VPN (99.99% SLA topology); Cloud Interconnect: Dedicated vs Partner; Cross-Cloud Interconnect (AWS/Azure direct multi-cloud links); Network Connectivity Center (NCC) router spoke integration; 99.9% vs 99.99% topologies; Direct Peering vs Carrier Peering
practice: Draw redundant VPN and Interconnect alternatives and remove one tunnel/link on paper; identify surviving routes and bandwidth.
exit_evidence: A hybrid ADR with separate failure domains, lead time and cost assumptions; a drawing does not prove an SLA.

title: BGP, MTU and NAT diagnosis
study: Cloud Router and BGP (dynamic route advertisement, MED, custom advertisements); Private Google Access for on-premises hosts; Choosing VPN vs Interconnect (bandwidth, latency, cost, SLA, lead time)
practice: Use supplied packet/route traces or an isolated lab to diagnose route withdrawal, asymmetric return traffic, MTU loss and NAT port pressure.
exit_evidence: An evidence-based diagnosis for each fault and a failover validation plan.

title: Object storage and local durability
study: Cloud Storage access and location choices, classes, lifecycle, Autoclass, versioning, retention/holds, Bucket Lock and signed access. Revisit filesystem flush/durable-write semantics from Day 10. One small bucket or local fixture is sufficient; irreversible retention locking is a design exercise.
practice: Upload a small synthetic dataset and test a narrow access path; inspect version/retention behavior without applying irreversible production locks.
exit_evidence: An object lifecycle/access worksheet and a durable-write versus cached-write explanation.

title: Transfers, block storage and restore
study: Transfer choices, checksums/reconciliation, replication and recovery; compare Storage Transfer Service, Transfer Appliance and BigQuery transfers. Contrast Persistent Disk, Hyperdisk and Local SSD at selection depth. Implement one copy/restore path, not every transfer product.
practice: Copy the small dataset with checksums; restore a local/database snapshot and compare record counts and application behavior.
exit_evidence: A reconciliation and restore report; compare transfer services and replication options on paper.

title: File systems and backup design
study: Filestore/NFS and block/file/object semantics; recognize Parallelstore and NetApp Volumes use cases. Backup and DR, snapshot schedules, application consistency and restore validation. Use current product documentation for tiers and availability rather than memorizing an unqualified list.
practice: Compare block, object and NFS access for the same workload; test a local file permission failure and plan one backup restore.
exit_evidence: A storage ADR and restore checklist with owner, retention and application-consistency checks.

title: Relational databases and transactions
study: Cloud SQL connection paths, pooling/limits, maintenance, backup/PITR, regional HA and cross-region replicas; compare AlloyDB compatibility/read pools at selection depth. Deep practice is one relational store: SQL isolation, locks/deadlocks, WAL/commit, durability and safe retry. Managed HA operation is revisited on Days 91–98.
practice: Run two concurrent local SQL transactions to observe one isolation/locking behavior; configure one small managed relational example only if a sandbox is available.
exit_evidence: SQL results, a connection/HA diagram and Cloud SQL-versus-AlloyDB comparison; no multi-database deployment requirement.

title: Distributed and nonrelational database choices
study: Spanner external consistency and regional/multi-region choices; Firestore document/index patterns; Bigtable wide-column/row-key/replication patterns. Introduce leader, quorum and consensus at diagram depth before discussing consistency and hotspotting. Compare schemas and failure behavior; implement only the selected store, with algorithm depth on Day 145.
practice: Compare Spanner, Firestore and Bigtable using the retailer's access patterns; model a hotspot and trace leader/replica/quorum behavior from public documentation.
exit_evidence: Three schema/key sketches, one selection ADR and an explicit consistency/failover assumption per option.

title: Caching, CDC and database selection
study: Memorystore/cache choices, stale reads and invalidation; Database Migration Service and Datastream/CDC. Compare database options against access patterns, scale, consistency and operational requirements. Advanced cache load behavior is Day 123; CDC correctness returns on Days 76 and 137.
practice: Add a tiny local cache or supplied fixture and observe a stale read; replay a small change stream and reconcile source/target counts.
exit_evidence: A cache invalidation timeline, CDC-lag explanation and completed database selection sheet.

title: Messaging, outbox and duplicate handling
study: Pub/Sub topic/subscription, push/pull, ordering, dead letters, retention/replay and exactly-once scope. Compare Tasks, Eventarc, Workflows, Application Integration and API gateway roles at recognition depth. Practise a local transaction/outbox, consumer deduplication, schema compatibility and crash/ack boundaries; contract governance returns on Day 167.
practice: Write one order plus an outbox record in a local transaction; deliver the event twice and verify the consumer changes business state once.
exit_evidence: A repeatable invariant check and crash-before/after-ack timeline; explain why transport delivery is not end-to-end exactly-once behavior.

title: Integrate one order-service path
study: Integrate a single selected runtime, datastore and message consumer for the retailer; preserve request IDs, identities and business invariants. Reuse network and health-check evidence instead of adding multiple new deployment paths.
practice: Connect one chosen runtime to one datastore and trace a request, response and fulfillment event; use local substitutes for services outside the budget.
exit_evidence: An end-to-end request/data/identity diagram with logs and one rejected unauthorized request.

title: Reproduce and recover the integrated baseline
study: Reproduce, diagnose and restore the integrated application. Use existing private-access, NAT, hybrid-routing and storage lifecycle artifacts to explain alternatives; a second runtime or paid hybrid deployment is optional after the required baseline succeeds.
practice: Rebuild the small baseline from recorded steps, introduce a single connection or consumer failure and recover it; compare alternate runtimes by diagram.
exit_evidence: A reproducibility log, recovery runbook and inventory/cleanup evidence rather than several new deployments.

title: Gate 3 — Operate the core application
study: Review and remediate prior material only; use the matching gate criteria in the Gates section. Do not introduce new services or concepts on a checkpoint day.
practice: Without the walkthrough, trace a request, diagnose one fault, recover the service and prove duplicate-event safety and access denial.
exit_evidence: A scored G3 decision and indexed operational evidence for later architecture choices.

title: Requirements from observed behavior
study: Business requirements: revenue goals, time-to-market, growth plans, risk appetite, geography, brand and customer experience; Technical requirements: throughput, latency, data volume, consistency, availability targets, integration points; Functional vs non-functional requirements (the "-ilities": availability, scalability, durability, maintainability, security, observability); Constraints: budget, existing contracts and licences, skills, legacy systems, regulatory limits, deadlines
practice: Turn the retailer's goals and earlier measurements into functional and nonfunctional requirements with explicit assumptions.
exit_evidence: A requirements register with units, acceptance methods and unresolved business questions.

title: Stakeholders and priority trade-offs
study: Stakeholder mapping (CTO, security, finance, operations, developers) and what each cares about; Questions a consultant asks in discovery (see the later discovery sessions on Days 146–151); Writing measurable requirements ("99.95% monthly availability", "p99 latency under 300 ms"); Prioritising with MoSCoW or weighted scoring
practice: Role-play conflicting finance, security and product requirements; prioritize them using a transparent weighting scheme.
exit_evidence: An agreed-priority simulation, stakeholder map and measurable success criteria.

title: Well-Architected review lenses
study: Operational excellence pillar (automation, monitoring, incident management, change management); Security, privacy and compliance pillar; Reliability pillar; Cost optimization pillar
practice: Review the application against operations, security, reliability and cost using existing artifacts rather than generic recommendations.
exit_evidence: One evidence-backed strength and one remediation per reviewed pillar.

title: Performance, sustainability and trade-offs
study: Performance optimization pillar; Sustainability pillar; system design as cross-cutting architectural guidance; How the pillars conflict (reliability costs money; security adds latency) and how to document trade-offs
practice: Add performance and sustainability review; change a region or redundancy assumption and recalculate its consequences.
exit_evidence: A six-pillar review with conflicting objectives and justified trade-offs.

title: Application architecture patterns
study: Three-tier web application; Static site and CDN; Microservices on GKE or Cloud Run with service-to-service authentication; Event-driven architecture (Pub/Sub, Eventarc, Dataflow)
practice: Redesign one synchronous operation as an event-driven workflow and identify the new state owner and failure cases.
exit_evidence: Before/after diagrams and an ADR linked to the Day 64 invariant.

title: Data and hybrid architecture vocabulary
study: Batch versus streaming, warehouse versus operational database, data lake/lakehouse, schema, event time and freshness; introductory pipeline/orchestration roles and data ownership. Compare API-first and hybrid integration. This prepares the practical data block beginning on Day 134.
practice: Sketch an order-to-analytics path and define batch/stream, event time, schema, lineage and ownership at introductory depth.
exit_evidence: A data-flow diagram and vocabulary sheet to be used in the later data labs.

title: Regional and tenant boundaries
study: Multi-region active-active vs active-passive; Multi-tenant SaaS designs (isolation by project, VPC, namespace or row); Landing zone / enterprise foundation (org structure, networking hub, shared VPC, logging, security baseline); Anti-patterns: lift-and-shift with no optimisation, single points of failure, chatty cross-region calls, giant monolithic projects
practice: Compare active/passive and active/active designs for two tenants; model a common dependency outage and data conflict.
exit_evidence: A topology ADR with isolation, recovery and write-ownership decisions.

title: Migration assessment and VMware fit
study: The 6 Rs: rehost, replatform, refactor, repurchase, retire, retain; Migration phases: assess, plan, deploy, optimise; Discovery and assessment tools: Migration Center, StratoZone-style inventory; Google Cloud VMware Engine: when retaining VMware is appropriate, private-cloud architecture, hybrid networking, migration dependencies, licensing and operational trade-offs.
practice: Inventory the small application, dependencies and licensing assumptions; compare rehost, replatform and refactor, including a VMware option.
exit_evidence: A migration assessment with one chosen route, two alternatives and unknowns requiring discovery.

title: Migration rehearsal and reconciliation
study: Cutover patterns, strangler modernization, transfer/CDC tools and network/DNS dependencies; reconciliation, lag, dual-write risk, acceptance thresholds and rollback boundaries. A small local data-migration rehearsal is required before final wave planning.
practice: Copy local synthetic records, replay changes, stop at cutover, validate counts/invariants and rehearse rollback.
exit_evidence: A timed cutover/rollback log, CDC-lag observation and reconciliation results; label simulation limits.

title: Migration waves and acceptance
study: Licensing considerations (Windows, SQL Server, Oracle); Application dependency mapping and wave planning; Rollback planning; Produce a migration rehearsal report covering reconciliation failures, rollback execution, data divergence during rollback, and business sign-off criteria.
practice: Use rehearsal evidence to sequence migration waves and define stop/go criteria, rollback boundaries and decommissioning.
exit_evidence: A migration wave plan with owners, licensing questions and business acceptance evidence.

title: Decision matrices grounded in experiments
study: Build vs buy vs managed service; Trade-off matrices with weighted criteria
practice: Compare two feasible architectures with weighted criteria and link each score to a measurement, source or labeled assumption.
exit_evidence: A decision matrix and sensitivity check showing when the preferred option changes.

title: ADRs, TCO and risk registers
study: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs): context, decision, consequences, alternatives; Total cost of ownership (TCO) comparisons; Risk registers (likelihood, impact, mitigation)
practice: Write an ADR and estimate a low/base/high TCO range; document one operational and one business risk.
exit_evidence: An ADR with alternatives, dated pricing assumptions and risk owners.

title: Architecture diagrams and failure sequences
study: C4 model (context, container, component); Network diagrams with regions, zones, subnets and flows; Data flow diagrams; Sequence diagrams for failure scenarios
practice: Create C4 context/container views and one failure sequence for the running retailer scenario.
exit_evidence: Consistent diagrams naming trust boundaries, state owners and failure responses.

title: First architecture defense
study: Architecture review, requirement traceability and changed-constraint reasoning. Reuse the C4/topology diagrams and migration rehearsal; defend one target architecture and revise its weakest ADR.
practice: Present the migration and target design, then respond to a changed budget or recovery requirement using prior lab evidence.
exit_evidence: A review memo with objections, revised ADR and measured-versus-assumed claims marked.

title: Gate 4 — Design from operational evidence
study: Review and remediate prior material only; use the matching gate criteria in the Gates section. Do not introduce new services or concepts on a checkpoint day.
practice: Audit three major decisions back to experiments or documented alternatives and repair one unsupported decision.
exit_evidence: A scored G4 result plus requirement-to-ADR-to-evidence traceability.

title: Availability math and dependency risk
study: Availability math: 99.9% vs 99.95% vs 99.99% downtime per month/year; Series vs parallel availability (composite SLA calculation: multiply for series dependencies); Single points of failure: identify and eliminate at every layer
practice: Calculate allowed downtime and series/parallel availability for a simplified topology; state independence assumptions explicitly.
exit_evidence: Correct calculations and a list of correlated failures excluded by the simple model.

title: Failure domains and graceful degradation
study: Failure domains: instance, zone, region, service, dependency, human error; HA vs fault tolerance vs disaster recovery vs backup (four distinct concepts); Graceful degradation and load shedding
practice: Remove a zone, dependency and operator credential in three tabletop scenarios and predict user-visible behavior.
exit_evidence: A failure matrix distinguishing availability, backup and regional recovery.

title: Retries, timeouts and overload vocabulary
study: Timeout/deadline budgets, bounded retry with jitter, idempotency, circuit breakers, bulkheads, load shedding and external state. Explain percentiles, arrival/service rates, queue depth and concurrency before applying capacity models; distinguish measured from forecast throughput.
practice: Replay a failing dependency locally with bounded retries and jitter; introduce queue length, arrival/service rates, concurrency and backpressure.
exit_evidence: A retry timeline and a request budget showing how duplicate work and amplification are controlled.

title: SLIs, SLOs and error budgets
study: SLIs, SLOs, SLAs and how they differ; Error budgets and how they govern release velocity; Toil and automation; Golden signals: latency, traffic, errors, saturation
practice: Choose request-based SLIs, calculate an error budget and define how its exhaustion changes release decisions.
exit_evidence: An SLO document with valid measurement window, exclusions and release policy.

title: Incidents, toil and capacity
study: Incident management: severity levels, on-call, escalation, incident commander; Blameless post-mortems; Capacity planning and load forecasting
practice: Run a short incident tabletop using the recovery runbook; forecast load and assign an incident commander and communication owner.
exit_evidence: An incident timeline, blameless action list and capacity assumptions.

title: Availability across infrastructure layers
study: **Compute:** regional MIGs across 3 zones, autohealing, over-provisioning for N+1, GKE regional clusters, multi-zone node pools, Pod Disruption Budgets, topology spread constraints; **Network:** redundant HA VPN tunnels, dual Interconnect in separate metros, redundant Cloud Routers, global load balancing with health checks; **Storage:** regional persistent disks, multi-region/dual-region buckets, Filestore regional/Enterprise; **Databases:** Cloud SQL HA + cross-region replicas, Spanner multi-region, Bigtable multi-cluster replication, Firestore multi-region, Memorystore Standard tier
practice: Check compute, network, storage and database failure boundaries against the SLO; model one zone loss and resource headroom.
exit_evidence: A layer-by-layer HA design with shared dependencies and capacity limits exposed.

title: Messaging, DNS and application health
study: **Messaging:** review Pub/Sub resource scope, regional endpoints, message storage policies and failure behavior; **DNS:** verify Cloud DNS SLA conditions and routing policies (geolocation, weighted, failover); **Application:** health check design (shallow vs deep), readiness vs liveness probes, graceful shutdown
practice: Simulate a stale DNS answer, unhealthy dependency and repeated message; verify readiness and graceful-shutdown behavior locally.
exit_evidence: A user-visible recovery timeline and a shallow-versus-deep health-check decision.

title: Recovery targets and patterns
study: RTO and RPO definitions and how business impact analysis produces them; DR patterns: backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby, hot standby / active-active; Cost vs RTO/RPO trade-off for each pattern
practice: Set business-derived RTO/RPO targets and compare backup/restore, warm standby and active configurations.
exit_evidence: A DR ADR with cost and recovery trade-offs grounded in earlier restore results.

title: Backups and replication correctness
study: Cold, warm and hot DR sites in hybrid setups; Backup strategies: snapshots, database backups, PITR, object versioning, cross-region copies, immutable backups; Backup and DR Service; Data replication: synchronous vs asynchronous and their RPO consequences
practice: Restore the synthetic dataset again after a new write; compare last committed, replicated and restored records.
exit_evidence: A recovery-point report distinguishing synchronous/asynchronous replication from backup retention.

title: Failover and failback planning
study: Failover and failback procedures, DNS TTL considerations; DR testing: tabletop exercises, game days, full failover drills; Verify quota scope and available failover capacity; rate-limiting and graceful degradation during regional brownouts; Runbooks and playbooks
practice: Walk failover and return-to-primary with route/DNS, identity, quota and data reconciliation checks; rehearse one step locally.
exit_evidence: An executable runbook with abort criteria, owner and consistency checks.

title: Metrics, alerting and burn rates
study: Cloud Monitoring: metrics, dashboards, metrics scopes (multi-project monitoring), custom metrics, Managed Service for Prometheus; Alerting policies: conditions, notification channels, incident lifecycle, alert fatigue, SLO-based burn-rate alerts; Uptime checks and synthetic monitoring
practice: Instrument request count, errors and latency or use a supplied metric dataset; trigger and clear one alert.
exit_evidence: A dashboard/metric definition and a correctly calculated burn-rate alert example.

title: Logs, traces and profiling
study: Cloud Logging: log buckets, log router, sinks (to BigQuery, Storage, Pub/Sub), exclusions, log-based metrics, retention, Log Analytics; Cloud Trace, Cloud Profiler, Error Reporting; OpenTelemetry instrumentation
practice: Propagate a request ID through the local service and consumer; correlate one slow request with logs and a trace/profile.
exit_evidence: A redacted diagnosis with timestamps, causal hypothesis and telemetry limitations.

title: Central observability and audit evidence
study: Ops Agent on VMs; Centralised logging design across projects and organisation-level aggregated sinks; Audit log types: Admin Activity, Data Access, System Event, Policy Denied
practice: Design aggregated logs and metric scopes; distinguish audit log types and decide retention and access for each.
exit_evidence: A telemetry ownership/retention plan and one query that identifies an authorization change.

title: Bounded failure experiment design
study: Load and stress testing (tools: k6, Locust, JMeter); Chaos engineering and fault injection (kill instances, block a zone, add latency); Canary and blue/green deployments; Game days and DR drills
practice: Write CPU, connection, duplicate-event and dependency-failure experiments with predictions, abort thresholds and recovery steps.
exit_evidence: An approved-for-lab experiment sheet; each experiment names expected signals and a preserved invariant.

title: Run a recovery and overload experiment
study: Performance baseline and regression analysis; apply the experiment plan to one bounded service failure or overload condition. Reuse a MIG autohealing example where available; use a supplied trace or tabletop for unavailable zonal failure tests and label the limits.
practice: Execute one bounded fault against the disposable service, measure latency/errors and restore it; use traces for unavailable zonal tests.
exit_evidence: Before/during/after evidence and a revised capacity/recovery model with simulation limits.

title: Restore and failover acceptance
study: Recovery acceptance after backup restore or replica promotion; verify data invariants, recovery time, loss and alert behavior. Compare Cloud SQL regional HA and cross-region promotion as separate scenarios; execute one representative recovery path and explain the alternative.
practice: Rehearse database restore or sandbox replica promotion and run application invariant checks afterward.
exit_evidence: Measured lab recovery time and data loss, a tested runbook and an explicit distinction from production RTO/RPO.

title: Advanced IAM and policy evaluation
study: Least privilege, separation of duties, need-to-know; Predefined vs custom roles; IAM Recommender for right-sizing permissions; IAM Conditions (time, resource, attribute-based); IAM Deny policies and Principal Access Boundaries
practice: Evaluate an allow/deny/condition fixture; test one least-privilege path and document effective access.
exit_evidence: An authorization decision matrix and a corrected excessive grant.

title: Workload federation and short-lived access
study: Organization Policy constraints (disable service account key creation, restrict resource locations, restrict external IPs, require OS Login, domain-restricted sharing); Service account best practices: one per workload, no keys, short-lived credentials, impersonation, service account token creator role; Workload Identity Federation (for external workloads like AWS, GitHub Actions, on-prem)
practice: Trace a worked external-workload federation flow and token exchange; test or simulate a bad audience/subject claim.
exit_evidence: A trust-boundary diagram with allowed/denied claims and no long-lived key requirement.

title: Workforce federation and remote access
study: Workforce Identity Federation (external IdPs for employees); Cloud Identity: SSO, SAML, 2-Step Verification, context-aware access; Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) for zero-trust access to apps and TCP forwarding to VMs
practice: Compare employee SSO with workload federation and trace an IAP access flow to a private resource.
exit_evidence: A human-access design with group membership, session and emergency-access assumptions.

title: Privileged access and break-glass
study: BeyondCorp / zero trust model; Privileged Access Manager (just-in-time elevation); Break-glass accounts; Access Transparency and Access Approval
practice: Tabletop a temporary privilege request and emergency recovery when the usual identity provider is unavailable.
exit_evidence: A time-bounded elevation and break-glass runbook with audit, revocation and accountable owner.

title: Defense in depth and network policy
study: Defence in depth layering; Firewall design patterns: tag/service-account-based rules, deny-by-default, hierarchical policies; Cloud Armor: preconfigured WAF rules (OWASP top 10), bot management, DDoS protection tiers, rate limiting; Private connectivity: no public IPs, Private Google Access, Private Service Connect, private GKE clusters
practice: Map a malicious request through edge, network, identity and application controls; test a harmless allow/deny fixture.
exit_evidence: A threat/control matrix with false-positive and bypass considerations.

title: Data perimeters and egress controls
study: VPC Service Controls: service perimeters, access levels, ingress/egress rules, dry-run mode (data exfiltration prevention); Cloud NGFW and Cloud IDS (intrusion detection); Secure Web Proxy
practice: Review VPC Service Controls dry-run violations or a supplied example; compare perimeter policy with firewall and IAM decisions.
exit_evidence: An exfiltration-path diagram and a staged enforcement plan with rollback.

title: Certificates, mTLS and hybrid encryption
study: TLS everywhere: managed certificates, mTLS, Certificate Authority Service; Secure hybrid connectivity: MACsec for Interconnect, HA VPN encryption; Bastion patterns vs IAP TCP forwarding; DNS security (DNSSEC, DNS logging)
practice: Validate a local certificate chain and rotate a test certificate; identify termination and encryption boundaries in the hybrid design.
exit_evidence: A rotation trace and ownership matrix explaining mTLS, DNSSEC and link versus end-to-end protection.

title: Data classification and key lifecycle
study: Data classification (public, internal, confidential, restricted); Encryption at rest (default Google-managed), CMEK (Cloud KMS), CSEK, external key manager (Cloud EKM); Encryption in transit and application-layer encryption; Cloud KMS: key rings, keys, versions, rotation, protection levels (software, HSM, external), key destruction
practice: Classify the synthetic dataset, map encryption choices and rehearse key-version rotation with a disposable or simulated key.
exit_evidence: A key lifecycle diagram with access, recovery and destruction safeguards; no irreversible destruction exercise.

title: Secrets and de-identification
study: Cloud HSM; Secret Manager: versions, rotation, access control, replication policy; Sensitive Data Protection (Cloud DLP): inspection, de-identification, tokenisation, masking
practice: Replace a test secret version and redact a synthetic sensitive field; confirm the application uses the new version.
exit_evidence: A rotation/revocation trace and before/after sanitized records without credentials in evidence.

title: Residency, confidentiality and data access
study: Confidential computing, resource location constraints, Assured Workloads and data sovereignty boundaries. Map retention/deletion/holds and column/row access with a synthetic local dataset; BigQuery enforcement is exercised in the data block on Day 135.
practice: Map storage, logs, backups and retrieval copies to locations; define row/column access rules using a local fixture.
exit_evidence: A data location/access matrix with deletion paths and limits of confidential-computing protection.

title: Compliance evidence and responsibility
study: Shared responsibility for compliance (Google's certifications do not make your workload compliant automatically); Standards to know at a conceptual level: ISO 27001, SOC 1/2/3, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, FedRAMP, NIST, CIS benchmarks, HITRUST; Compliance resource centre and compliance reports manager
practice: Choose one fictional regulatory context and map its stated obligations to controls, owners and evidence sources.
exit_evidence: A control/evidence register that distinguishes provider certifications from workload obligations.

title: Policy as code and audit retention
study: Assured Workloads (compliance regimes as guardrails); Audit logging design: Admin Activity (always on), Data Access (enable selectively), log retention, log integrity, sinks to locked buckets; Policy as code: Organization Policy, Config Controller, Policy Controller (OPA/Gatekeeper), Terraform Sentinel-style checks; Data protection regulations: right to erasure, data minimisation, breach notification, DPA and SCCs
practice: Evaluate a supplied policy rule against compliant/noncompliant resource plans and verify both results.
exit_evidence: A versioned policy test and audit-retention design with an exception owner.

title: Regulated workload design
study: PCI-DSS design: cardholder data environment isolation, tokenisation, segmentation; HIPAA design: BAA, PHI handling, audit controls; Vendor and third-party risk basics
practice: Adapt the retailer into one synthetic payments or health scenario; define isolation, data minimization and vendor boundaries.
exit_evidence: A regulated-workload ADR and evidence gaps for a qualified compliance review; no claim of legal certification.

title: Threat detection and triage
study: Security Command Center (Standard vs Premium vs Enterprise): findings, misconfiguration detection, threat detection, attack path simulation; Google SecOps (Chronicle SIEM & SOAR architecture); Mandiant Threat Intelligence integration; Event Threat Detection, Container Threat Detection, Web Security Scanner; Vulnerability management: OS patch management, Artifact Analysis, GKE security posture
practice: Triage a supplied SCC/SecOps finding, correlate relevant logs and decide severity and containment scope.
exit_evidence: A finding-to-incident record with evidence preserved and false-positive checks.

title: Incident response and threat modelling
study: Incident response process: detect, contain, eradicate, recover, learn; Forensics basics: snapshots, log preservation, evidence handling; Threat modelling (STRIDE) on your own architecture; Penetration testing rules on GCP
practice: Run a STRIDE review and an incident tabletop through detection, containment, recovery and lessons learned.
exit_evidence: A threat model, incident timeline and owners for the highest residual risks.

title: Artifact integrity and admission
study: Secure SDLC and shift-left security; Artifact Registry with vulnerability scanning; Binary Authorization and attestations
practice: Build a tiny image, inspect its scan/provenance evidence and evaluate an admission policy fixture for trusted versus untrusted artifacts.
exit_evidence: An artifact digest, findings triage and accept/reject decision with an exception procedure.

title: Container and pipeline hardening
study: SLSA levels, software supply chain concepts, SBOMs; Secrets in CI/CD (never in code or images); Container hardening (distroless images, non-root users, read-only filesystems)
practice: Run the local image as non-root with restricted filesystem permissions; remove a test embedded secret and verify the failure mode.
exit_evidence: A hardened manifest/image diff and explanation of SBOM, provenance and remaining runtime risks.

title: Integrate private access and key controls
study: Integrate controls already studied: no-public-IP access, IAP, private API access, policy guardrails, perimeter dry-run and CMEK rotation. Validate the existing example end to end; optional separate bucket/database deployments must fit the lab budget.
practice: Re-test the established private access, perimeter and key-rotation controls as one request path; use saved sandbox artifacts rather than deploying everything anew.
exit_evidence: An integrated security trace and a list of inconsistencies repaired across identity, network and data controls.

title: Security handover and evidence repair
study: Consolidate synthetic-data de-identification, aggregate-log design, IAM-change alerts and threat-model evidence from earlier days. Repair one missing control test and prepare the regulated-workload handover.
practice: Repeat one denied-access test and the sanitized-data flow; review logging coverage and update the regulated capstone risk register.
exit_evidence: A security evidence index, supported claims and unresolved risks with owners.

title: Gate 5 — Reliability and security acceptance
study: Review and remediate prior material only; use the matching gate criteria in the Gates section. Do not introduce new services or concepts on a checkpoint day.
practice: Replay a recovery and an unauthorized-access scenario; verify the data invariant and inspect the incident/control evidence.
exit_evidence: A scored G5 decision; failed access isolation, recovery or correctness must be repaired before passing.

title: Cost baseline and commitments
study: FinOps principles: inform, optimise, operate; showback vs chargeback; Cost visibility: labels, billing export to BigQuery, Looker Studio dashboards, budgets and alerts, anomaly detection; Compute savings: rightsizing recommendations, idle resource recommender, Spot VMs for fault-tolerant workloads, committed use discounts (resource-based vs spend-based/flexible), sustained use discounts, scheduling start/stop for non-prod
practice: Build a cost baseline from billing data or a supplied export and compare rightsizing, Spot and commitment options with the same usage assumptions.
exit_evidence: A dated cost model with fixed/variable costs, utilization uncertainty and commitment risk.

title: Storage, network and database costs
study: Storage savings: storage class selection, lifecycle rules, Autoclass, deleting orphaned disks and snapshots; Network savings: egress costs (inter-region, internet, inter-zone), CDN offload, Premium vs Standard tier, keeping traffic in-region; Database savings: rightsizing, committed use for Cloud SQL, Spanner processing units instead of nodes, Bigtable autoscaling
practice: Calculate costs for two storage/egress/replication designs and identify idle resources from the inventory.
exit_evidence: A savings proposal with performance/recovery consequences and no double-counted savings.

title: Runtime, analytics and carbon cost drivers
study: Runtime utilization, scale-to-zero/concurrency, cluster packing and autoscaling cost drivers. Introduce query bytes scanned, partition pruning and capacity pricing using supplied examples before the BigQuery lab; review Carbon Footprint boundaries and low-carbon placement assumptions.
practice: Use supplied query scan estimates and runtime metrics to compare serverless/GKE cost drivers; introduce carbon reporting boundaries.
exit_evidence: A cost-driver worksheet and explicit estimates to validate in the later BigQuery lab.

title: Unit economics and sensitivity
study: Pricing Calculator: build a full estimate for every design; Unit economics (cost per user, per transaction, per request); Cost vs reliability trade-off decisions
practice: Calculate cost per order at three traffic levels and change a retention or availability assumption.
exit_evidence: A low/base/high unit-cost model and a defensible optimization priority.

title: Caching correctness under load
study: Diagnose caching as one possible bottleneck: cache-aside/write-through, TTL/invalidation, stale-data tolerance, hot keys and stampedes. Compare CDN, application cache, Memorystore and BI Engine at selection depth. Revisit CPU/memory/I/O evidence; assisted diagnostics returns on Day 168.
practice: Measure cache hits/misses locally, expire a hot key and test one stampede mitigation while checking stale-data tolerance.
exit_evidence: Latency/load results, cache-aside versus write-through comparison and an invalidation ADR.

title: Database, network and I/O bottlenecks
study: Database performance: indexing, query plans, connection pooling, read replicas, sharding, Spanner schema and key design, Bigtable row key design; Network performance: Premium tier, regional placement near users, HTTP/3, connection reuse, compression; Disk performance selection (IOPS and throughput limits scale with size and vCPU count); Asynchronous processing to smooth spikes (queues, Pub/Sub)
practice: Compare one query plan before/after an index and one bounded connection-pool setting; use traces to distinguish network versus disk waits.
exit_evidence: A controlled before/after report with unchanged correctness and workload assumptions.

title: Profiling and capacity evidence
study: Profiling with Cloud Profiler and Trace; Load testing to size systems; Right-sizing GPUs/TPUs for ML workloads
practice: Profile the same workload and estimate headroom; review a supplied accelerator-sizing example without provisioning a cluster.
exit_evidence: A bottleneck diagnosis and capacity recommendation separating measurements from projections.

title: Terraform baseline and state boundaries
study: Terraform providers/resources/variables/outputs/modules and plan/apply; state, environments, remote GCS locking/versioning/access, imports and version pinning. Build one minimal module. Recognize Foundation Toolkit, Config Connector and Config Sync; drift/recovery/testing follows on Day 127.
practice: Read an annotated minimal module, pin versions and create a small disposable resource or local test; inspect the plan and remote-state access design.
exit_evidence: Versioned IaC, plan/recreation evidence and an environment/state isolation diagram with sensitive values redacted.

title: Terraform testing, drift and recovery
study: State recovery, drift reconciliation, safe import, validation, policy checks and Terraform tests. Compare GitOps, Infrastructure Manager, Ansible/Packer and legacy Deployment Manager awareness without implementing each tool. Recover only disposable test state, never a shared production backend.
practice: Change one disposable resource out of band, detect drift and test correction; rehearse state recovery with a test state copy and validate a policy/test fixture.
exit_evidence: A drift/recovery runbook, passing validation evidence and documented locking/versioning assumptions.

title: Build and deployment pipeline
study: Source: Cloud Source Repositories alternatives (GitHub, GitLab), branching strategies; Cloud Build: triggers, build steps, private pools, caching, substitutions; Artifact Registry: repositories, cleanup policies, remote and virtual repositories; Cloud Deploy: delivery pipelines, targets, promotion, approvals, rollbacks
practice: Create a minimal build/test/deploy pipeline for the established service or execute its local equivalent; retain artifact digests and narrow identities.
exit_evidence: A reproducible pipeline run and staged-promotion diagram; identify where a managed deployment target is required.

title: Release rollback and delivery measures
study: Rolling, blue/green, canary and feature-flag release choices; unit/integration/security/load-test responsibilities, least-privilege pipeline identity and delivery metrics. Execute one bad-revision rollback. Compare emulator and disposable-cloud verification, documenting what each can establish.
practice: Introduce a bad application revision, catch it in tests or canary checks and roll back; compare emulator and cloud integration boundaries.
exit_evidence: A rollback trace and correctly defined delivery metrics with measured/simulated values labeled.

title: Service catalog and ownership
study: Operating model: who owns what (platform team vs product teams); Change management and release governance; Incident, problem and change processes (ITIL awareness); Runbook automation; Service catalog and self-service provisioning: approved templates, ownership, supported configurations, provisioning workflows and lifecycle management.
practice: Package the proven baseline as one supported platform offering with inputs, owners, service boundaries and provisioning steps.
exit_evidence: A catalog entry and operating responsibility matrix linked to the IaC/pipeline evidence.

title: Lifecycle, exceptions and adoption
study: Resource ownership, tagging, expiry and cleanup; policy guardrails, business continuity and team skills. Introduce shared-failure/blast-radius analysis, staged policy rollout, platform funding and exception expiry before the later multi-team architecture sessions.
practice: Review a team's request for a nonstandard runtime and define an exception with expiry, funding, cleanup and training requirements.
exit_evidence: An exception decision and resource lifecycle policy with named review triggers.

title: Customer success and platform outcomes
study: Customer success, adoption KPIs, support readiness, acceptance, handover and post-launch reviews. Use a supplied billing export/dashboard if no data exists; do not require the later warehouse lab as an unstated prerequisite.
practice: Define adoption, support readiness and unit-cost measures; evaluate a supplied billing export/dashboard and handover checklist.
exit_evidence: A customer-success plan with measurable acceptance criteria, owner and post-launch review date.

title: Operations integration and remediation
study: Integrate the IaC, release, recovery and cost evidence from Days 119–132. Validate one feasible saving while preserving correctness and SLO assumptions; prioritize remediation. Full-stack rebuilds and multiple fresh deployments are not additional same-day assignments.
practice: Recreate only the small baseline from existing IaC, check rollback evidence and validate the best cost improvement under the same workload; repair missing evidence.
exit_evidence: A release/recovery/cost acceptance pack and draft rescue capstone; no arbitrary savings percentage target.

title: Warehouse foundations and query costs
study: BigQuery storage/compute separation, datasets, partitions/clusters, batch/stream ingestion, Storage Write API, external tables/BigLake, materialized views and BI Engine. Use one tiny aggregation to investigate correctness and query-cost drivers; internal architecture names are recognition-level.
practice: Load a tiny synthetic order dataset into a sandbox warehouse or local equivalent; compare an aggregate with source totals and estimate scan cost.
exit_evidence: A verified query result, partition/cluster rationale and explicit limits of a local substitute.

title: Warehouse security and reporting
study: Pricing models: on-demand vs capacity (editions, slots, autoscaling); Security: IAM, column/row-level security, policy tags, authorised views, CMEK; BigQuery ML, scheduled queries, data transfer service; Looker and Looker Studio for BI
practice: Test or simulate one permitted and one denied data view and create a small cost/quality report.
exit_evidence: A row/column access decision and report with source totals reconciled.

title: Batch and streaming processing choices
study: Batch versus stream processing, Beam windows/watermarks and late data; compare Dataflow, Dataproc/Spark, Composer, Data Fusion, Dataform and Workflows by responsibility. Implement one local transform; managed engine deployments are alternatives, not cumulative lab requirements.
practice: Run one local batch transformation; explain event time, windows and watermarks with a worked late-event example; compare managed engine roles on paper.
exit_evidence: A reproducible transform and engine-selection matrix with freshness/cost requirements.

title: Streaming correctness and CDC
study: Pub/Sub to Dataflow to BigQuery streaming pattern; Datastream for real-time change data capture (CDC); Event-driven stream processing, exactly-once processing guarantees, and dead-letter queues; Lab: replay duplicate and out-of-order events, evolve an event schema, and verify consumer deduplication and dead-letter recovery without duplicate business effects.
practice: Replay duplicate, late and out-of-order events into the local/sandbox pipeline and introduce an incompatible schema version.
exit_evidence: Invariant and aggregate checks, a dead-letter recovery procedure and safe replay/compatibility rules.

title: Lakehouse and open table design
study: Cloud Storage as data lake foundation (raw, curated, consumption zones); File formats: Parquet, Avro, ORC; Lakehouse architecture with BigLake and open table formats (Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, Hudi); Object table metadata
practice: Write a small columnar dataset or inspect a supplied file manifest; compare raw/curated/consumption zones and open table formats.
exit_evidence: A storage/table-format decision with ownership, retention and schema-evolution requirements.

title: Catalogs, lineage and data contracts
study: Knowledge Catalog and legacy Dataplex terminology: distinguish current catalog/discovery capabilities from older lake/zone/asset designs; data profiling and quality tasks; Data lineage tracking across BigQuery and Dataflow; Policy tags, fine-grained access control (column/row-level security); Data mesh contracts
practice: Trace one field from source through analytics to an optional retrieval index; define quality, freshness, access and deletion obligations.
exit_evidence: A versioned data contract and lineage/access diagram with responsible producers and consumers.

title: ML lifecycle and model selection
study: Training versus inference, labels/features, model registry/version, endpoints and pipelines; introduce drift and MLOps evaluation. Compare prebuilt Search/Conversation/Vision/Image/Video/Audio APIs, Model Garden and custom models. Explain embeddings, retrieval, grounding and evaluation vocabulary using a worked request flow before Day 141; custom training and feature-store deployment are optional.
practice: Use a worked model lifecycle to distinguish training, serving and evaluation; compare one prebuilt API, one Model Garden option and custom training. Prepare ten synthetic evaluation cases.
exit_evidence: A model selection sheet and versioned evaluation dataset including forbidden, absent and stale information; no custom training requirement.

title: Build a small grounded-answer flow
study: A single RAG request path: ingestion, chunking, embeddings, indexing, permission-aware retrieval, reranking, grounding and context caching. Choose one small managed or mocked implementation and a fixed model/prompt version; compare Search/Vector Search alternatives at design depth.
practice: Use a supplied starter or local mock to ingest a tiny corpus, retrieve permitted passages and return a grounded answer; compare two chunk/retrieval settings.
exit_evidence: Retrieval/answer results for ten cases, citations, latency/cost observations and explicit mock limitations.

title: Bounded tools and enterprise assistants
study: Workflow versus agent, function/tool execution, tool identity, human approval and bounded retries. Compare Gemini Enterprise, Agent Platform and enterprise notebooks against current terminology; recognize ReAct, multi-agent and LangChain/LlamaIndex alternatives without requiring several frameworks.
practice: Add one read-only tool or deterministic simulation, test its identity and duplicate call, and compare workflow versus agent and enterprise assistant/notebook options.
exit_evidence: A tool authorization boundary, repeated-call result and product-fit ADR; consequential actions remain simulated behind approval.

title: AI security and evaluation
study: Model Armor, prompt/response sanitization, groundedness/quality/safety evaluation and auditability. Reuse the established corpus/tool and ten-case evaluation set; separate application-enforced permissions from model behavior and document residual risks.
practice: Run the fixed evaluation set against unauthorized retrieval, injection and unsafe tool requests; exercise refusal/fallback and inspect redacted traces.
exit_evidence: Scored quality/security results, residual risks and enforceable token/tool limits; do not treat a model filter as the authorization boundary.

title: AI serving and infrastructure choices
study: AI Hypercomputer compute/storage/network integration, managed versus self-managed serving, GPU/TPU selection, scheduling/reservations and vLLM/Triton roles. Treat specific accelerator generations and RoCE/GPUDirect as current-documentation awareness. Reuse measured request results for a paper sizing exercise, deployment/monitoring design and rollback plan.
practice: Compare managed serving with a supplied GPU/TPU capacity scenario; reuse evaluation results to choose latency/cost/availability targets and an upgrade rollback.
exit_evidence: An AI deployment ADR, sizing assumptions, model/version rollback and evaluation acceptance criteria; no cluster deployment.

title: Distributed state and regional correctness
study: CAP/PACELC trade-offs, public Spanner/TrueTime consistency behavior, leader/quorum/consensus, Paxos/Raft at explanatory depth, two-phase commit versus saga compensation and partition tolerance. Tie each concept to earlier state, duplicate-event and recovery evidence; implementing consensus is optional specialist work.
practice: Replay an interrupted state transition and compare saga compensation, two-phase commit and idempotent retry; discuss consensus and partition trade-offs from public sources.
exit_evidence: A correctness/failure ADR grounded in duplicate, migration and recovery evidence rather than assumed managed internals.

title: Case analysis and discovery method
