study: The 6-step discovery method: Business drivers, Technical constraints, Architecture trade-offs, Target GCP topology, Security & Compliance, Cost/Operations. Note: Focus on current active cases (EHR, Altostrat, Cymbal, KnightMotives); Mountkirk/TerramEarth/HRL are retired legacy cases.
practice: Apply the six-step discovery method to the retailer before opening an official case; separate stated facts, assumptions and design options.
exit_evidence: A reusable case worksheet covering business, constraints, trade-offs, topology, security and operations.

title: Extract facts and numeric requirements
study: Underline every number (users, RPS, TB, latency, RTO/RPO, budget); Underline every adjective that hides a requirement ("global", "regulated", "spiky", "legacy", "real-time"); Separate stated needs from implied needs
practice: Read one official case and highlight quantities, constraints and ambiguities without proposing products yet.
exit_evidence: A fact/assumption register with every claim traceable to the case source.

title: Map requirements and conflicts
study: Map each requirement to a GCP capability; Spot the "watchpoints" (conflicting requirements, hidden compliance needs, skill gaps); Note what is explicitly out of scope
practice: Connect each requirement to two candidate capabilities and identify conflicting goals and scope exclusions.
exit_evidence: A requirements-to-options matrix and questions that would change the design.

title: Discovery: business, load and recovery
study: What is the business driver for this project?; What are the availability, RTO and RPO targets, and what does an hour of downtime cost?; What are peak and average load, and how spiky is it?
practice: Role-play customer answers for the retailer's availability, traffic and business-impact questions; revise its SLO assumptions.
exit_evidence: A discovery transcript or self-review with quantified requirements and unresolved questions.

title: Discovery: data, regulation and skills
study: Where are users, and where must data legally reside?; What regulations and audits apply?; What existing systems must we integrate with?; What skills does the team have?
practice: Map users, data locations, integrations and operator skills; identify where a proposed architecture exceeds team capabilities.
exit_evidence: A constraint/skills matrix and a mitigation or simpler alternative for each gap.

title: Discovery: budget, risks and success
study: What is the budget and the timeline?; What are the biggest risks as the customer sees them?; How will success be measured?
practice: Negotiate a budget/time constraint in the simulation and rank risks and measurable outcomes.
exit_evidence: A scoped proposal with acceptance criteria and explicit exclusions.

title: EHR Healthcare — facts and migration constraints
study: Read the current EHR case through the official exam guide. Separate its stated requirements from assumptions about compliance, database targets, hybrid topology and managed runtimes; evaluate migration and recovery constraints before selecting services.
practice: Read the current EHR case through the official guide; extract actual application, database, security and migration constraints.
exit_evidence: A source-linked fact register with inferred product choices clearly labeled as proposals.

title: EHR Healthcare — defend the design
study: Compare proposed database/runtime/connectivity, least-privilege, encryption and audit designs against actual EHR requirements. Record alternatives rather than treating Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Spanner or GKE as a prescribed answer.
practice: Compare two migration/recovery designs against EHR's stated requirements and rehearse one failure scenario.
exit_evidence: A one-page design, ADR, cost assumptions and risk list; update the regulated and migration capstones with transferable lessons.

title: Altostrat Media — content and AI requirements
study: Read the official case; extract media summarization, metadata enrichment, content safety and conversational-support requirements. Identify existing platform components and distinguish facts from proposed solutions.
practice: Extract hybrid content, discovery, summarization, safety and operating requirements from the official case.
exit_evidence: A source-linked requirements matrix and existing-versus-proposed system diagram.

title: Altostrat Media — architecture defense
study: Compare designs for AI-assisted discovery and support, hybrid Kubernetes delivery, CI/CD, storage cost and auditable AI decisions. Record alternatives and evaluation criteria; CDN/transcoding choices are supporting design options, not the complete case.
practice: Compare two content/AI integration options using the earlier retrieval evaluation and delivery evidence.
exit_evidence: An ADR covering quality, auditability, hybrid operations and cost with one rejected option.

title: Cymbal Retail — catalog and commerce requirements
study: Read the official case; capture supplier-data integration, product attribute/description/image generation, product discovery, conversational commerce and human review before catalog publication.
practice: Read the official case and identify supplier integration, generated content, product discovery and human-review needs.
exit_evidence: A fact register and content approval/data-flow diagram with security boundaries.

title: Cymbal Retail — architecture defense
study: Compare secure modernization of legacy file/ETL integrations, databases and container workloads. Design review/approval, observability and quality checks; justify each database choice rather than assuming Spanner or a seasonal-traffic requirement.
practice: Design a review-before-publication path and conversational discovery flow; test a failure or rejection using synthetic content.
exit_evidence: A one-page design with quality/approval acceptance criteria, integration alternatives and cost assumptions.

title: KnightMotives — modernization requirements
study: Read the official case; identify fragmented vehicle software, unreliable ordering, legacy mainframe/ERP, dealer constraints, plant/rural connectivity and the five-year customer-experience transformation.
practice: Extract ordering, dealer, legacy-system, connectivity, AI, privacy and skills constraints from the official case.
exit_evidence: A source-linked dependency map and prioritized business outcomes.

title: KnightMotives — architecture defense
study: Compare hybrid modernization, dealer tooling, protected data monetization, AI/ML and simulation infrastructure. Include privacy, incident response, skills and funding; justify telemetry services as options rather than treating IoT analytics as the whole case.
practice: Sequence modernization waves and compare connectivity/data/AI options while handling a stopped wave and limited dealer resources.
exit_evidence: A phased design with rollback, funding, privacy and adoption risks linked to case facts.

title: Case synthesis and feedback
study: Review the four previously prepared official case packages for requirement traceability, cost, failure behavior and evidence. Correct the weakest package and transfer useful findings into the five capstones.
practice: Review the four existing case packages for contradictions and unsupported assumptions; revise the weakest design rather than recreating all four.
exit_evidence: A corrected case portfolio and an evidence-based error log for exam review.

title: Changed-constraint design exercise
study: Choose one fictional scenario from retail, healthcare, payments, gaming, media, IoT, government, SaaS or manufacturing. Time-box its initial design, change one constraint and review all six pillars. Additional scenarios are optional.
practice: Choose one new fictional scenario, defend a design in 30 minutes, then change one cost, residency or recovery constraint.
exit_evidence: A before/after ADR and six-pillar critique; other fictional scenarios are optional extensions.

title: Exam domain mapping and sample questions
study: Read the current official standard-exam guide and weights, distinguish renewal scope, and map all six domains to evidence. Use official sample questions and legitimate practice materials; record why wrong answers fail the stated requirements.
practice: Map evidence to all six current standard-exam domains, answer official sample questions and analyze every error.
exit_evidence: A source-dated exam map and remediation list; a sample score is not proof of readiness.

title: Timed reasoning and source-backed limits
study: Build flash cards for service limits, decision rules and SLAs; Practise elimination: remove options that violate a stated requirement; Watch for keywords: "minimum operational overhead" (managed/serverless), "lowest cost" (Spot, lifecycle, committed use), "global" (Spanner, global LB), "least privilege", "without changing code", "near real time"; Time management drills (the exam is long, so practise pacing)
practice: Complete a timed set of legitimate practice questions; justify eliminations and verify uncertain limits in current documentation.
exit_evidence: An error log separating knowledge gaps, misread requirements and timing issues, with corrective study links.

title: Readiness plan and remaining repairs
study: Remediate the weakest domain, inspect official preparation and booking requirements, and maintain a readiness plan. Booking is a learner decision after evidence review; Days 165–179 still contain required work and Day 180 is the light-review/rest day.
practice: Repair the weakest exam domain using existing lab/design artifacts; review booking requirements and schedule only when ready.
exit_evidence: A readiness decision and remaining learning plan; final light review belongs on Day 180, not before platform work.

title: Landing zones and multi-team platform boundaries
study: Multi-project landing zone design: automated Project Vending Machine / Project Factory; Shared VPC topology across business units; Centralized egress and ingress inspection; Hierarchical Organization Policies and service control guardrails; Tenant isolation and billing boundaries; Connect the service catalog to a project provisioning workflow with approved Terraform templates, ownership metadata, budgets and guardrail validation.
practice: Review onboarding a second team through the service catalog, project factory and shared network; model one shared-policy failure and staged rollback.
exit_evidence: A platform standard with owner, rollout rings, blast radius, exception expiry and adoption measures.

title: Production identity across teams
study: Application Default Credentials (ADC) resolution order; Workload Identity Federation (WIF) with AWS, Azure, GitHub Actions, and on-premises Kubernetes; Service account impersonation vs long-lived keys; Short-lived access tokens, downscoping tokens, and service-to-service mTLS
practice: Trace an external workload into the platform and model issuer outage, audience mismatch and emergency access; check credential lifecycle ownership.
exit_evidence: A federation/delegation standard with redacted test/fixture evidence and recovery authority.

title: API contracts and compatibility
study: Apigee X architecture: API gateway, developer portal, traffic management, rate limiting, and analytics; Cloud Endpoints and API Gateway; gRPC and Protocol Buffers for low-latency internal microservices; API versioning, backward compatibility, and contract testing
practice: Change a sample API/event schema; run contract fixtures for old/new consumers and rehearse a compatibility-window rollback.
exit_evidence: A versioned contract, pass/fail results and cross-team migration/ownership plan.

title: Sustainability and assisted operations
study: Carbon Footprint dashboard; Low-carbon region selection and carbon-free energy percentages (CFE%); Carbon-aware batch and workload scheduling; Gemini Cloud Assist for AIOps: natural language incident diagnostics, automated root-cause investigation, and assisted Terraform generation
practice: Compare two placement/scheduling options with stated carbon/cost assumptions; review an AI-generated or supplied incident hypothesis against real evidence.
exit_evidence: A sustainability ADR and accepted/rejected diagnostic claims with human accountability and source limits.

title: Capacity allocation and overload governance
study: Service-specific quota scopes, shared allocation policy and reservations; verify available capacity in each failover region; Rate limiting and adaptive concurrency limits; Graceful degradation under saturation: load shedding, feature flags, degraded responses, and queuing backpressure; Service-level quota monitoring and automated quota alerts
practice: Model two teams competing for shared quota during regional failure; apply priority, backpressure and load-shedding rules and replay a bounded overload fixture.
exit_evidence: A capacity/continuity standard with reserved headroom, measurable triggers and an owner for exceptions.

title: Compute and database decision synthesis
study: Synthesis: Compute Engine vs GKE vs Cloud Run vs Cloud Functions vs AI Hypercomputer; Database selection tree: Cloud SQL vs AlloyDB vs Cloud Spanner vs Firestore vs Cloud Bigtable; Multi-tenant vs single-tenant database partitioning
practice: Revisit the runtime/database ADRs with a changed tenant or consistency requirement and compare two feasible combinations.
exit_evidence: Updated decision matrices linked to operational evidence and clearly stated rejection reasons.

title: Network decision synthesis
study: Synthesis: Global vs Regional Load Balancers; Hybrid connectivity decision tree: HA VPN vs Dedicated/Partner Interconnect vs Cross-Cloud Interconnect vs NCC; Private Service Connect (PSC) vs VPC Peering vs Private Services Access (PSA)
practice: Defend load-balancer, hybrid and private-service choices for a new region and overlapping customer network.
exit_evidence: A topology and connectivity ADR with failure paths, ownership and rollout/rollback requirements.

title: Storage, messaging and limits synthesis
study: Compare object/file/block storage and Pub/Sub/Kafka/Tasks/Eventarc with retention, ordering and replay requirements. Treat Pub/Sub Lite as deprecation/migration awareness. Verify each selected SLA, limit, region and topology condition with a dated source rather than memorizing generic availability numbers.
practice: Select storage and messaging for a changed retention/replay requirement and verify applicable SLA conditions and quotas from current sources.
exit_evidence: A dated decision sheet distinguishing contractual SLA, design SLO, quota and physical capacity.

title: Consulting, portfolio and customer handover
study: Consulting communication: stakeholder alignment, exec summaries, navigating trade-offs; Architecture Decision Records (ADRs): context, decision, consequences; Deliverable catalog: High-Level Design (HLD), Low-Level Design (LLD), Risk Register, Migration Wave Plan; Customer handover: acceptance evidence, runbooks, support ownership, adoption goals and post-launch review. Prepare portfolio structure and case walkthroughs; consolidate operating rules, lab evidence and progress tracking for the final checkpoint.
practice: Prepare technical and executive handovers from existing artifacts and defend one disputed decision to a simulated stakeholder.
exit_evidence: Five draft capstone packages with owners, measurable acceptance, exceptions and evidence indexes; identify any gaps before the gate.

title: Gate 6 — Integrated readiness and remediation
study: Review and remediate prior material only; use the matching gate criteria in the Gates section. Do not introduce new services or concepts on a checkpoint day.
practice: Audit all 83 topics against evidence; re-run the weakest practical check and critique one unsupported cross-team policy.
exit_evidence: A scored G6 decision, complete topic tracker and no unresolved critical correctness, access or recovery failures.

title: Capstone 1 — Landing-zone defense
study: Synthesize the existing capstone package and address review findings. Reuse the earlier experiments and designs; this day is a defense and acceptance review, not a new implementation project.
practice: Defend the existing platform package, then handle a new-team request and a shared-policy outage with staged recovery.
exit_evidence: Final HLD/LLD, ADRs, cost/risk model and scored review; onboarding, exception and recovery ownership must be explicit.

title: Capstone 2 — Regulated-workload defense
study: Synthesize the existing capstone package and address review findings. Reuse the earlier experiments and designs; this day is a defense and acceptance review, not a new implementation project.
practice: Defend the regulated package and simulate unauthorized access, a deletion request and incident evidence collection.
exit_evidence: Final design/control/evidence package with residual risks, retention/deletion handling and a qualified-review boundary.

title: Capstone 3 — Global-application defense
study: Synthesize the existing capstone package and address review findings. Reuse the earlier experiments and designs; this day is a defense and acceptance review, not a new implementation project.
practice: Defend the availability target, then model a regional failure with data, routing and capacity constraints.
exit_evidence: Final design and recovery model with lab evidence distinguished from production guarantees and common-cause risk included.

title: Capstone 4 — Migration defense
study: Synthesize the existing capstone package and address review findings. Reuse the earlier experiments and designs; this day is a defense and acceptance review, not a new implementation project.
practice: Defend the wave plan and replay cutover rejection, reconciliation and rollback using the earlier rehearsal.
exit_evidence: Final migration package with measurable acceptance, source/target invariants, owners and decommissioning criteria.

title: Capstone 5 — Cost and reliability rescue
study: Synthesize the existing capstone package and address review findings. Reuse the earlier experiments and designs; this day is a defense and acceptance review, not a new implementation project.
practice: Defend the rescue package under a reduced budget while preserving declared SLO and correctness requirements.
exit_evidence: Final before/after cost/reliability model, trade-off ADRs, adoption plan and scored review with honest uncertainty.

title: Final review, logistics and rest
study: Consolidate existing evidence, logistics and the continuing-learning plan. No new material.
practice: Read the remaining uncertainty log, confirm exam arrangements if booked and stop adding new scope.
exit_evidence: A continuing-learning list, verified cleanup and realistic next steps; no new lab or timed assessment.
